transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mrs. Al-Rashid. How are you feeling now that you are awake?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very tired. And my stomach... it hurts. Why did I have to go back to the operating room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it has been a very scary few hours for you. There was a situation that occurred with your medication which led to some bleeding, and that is why the surgeons had to intervene.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Medication? I thought I was getting the medicine to help my blood. What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was a bit of a mix-up with the dosing process. Things didn't go quite right with how the order was processed in the system, and you ended up receiving more than was intended.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: More? Do you mean it was a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an issue with the administration. The system can be quite complex, and sometimes errors in the electronic records can happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You are the doctor. You are supposed to make sure I get the right amount. Did I almost die?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're upset. We are monitoring you very closely now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not just upset. I am frightened. I trusted you all. How could this happen in a hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the important thing is that the surgeons were able to stop the bleeding quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen? Was it the nurse? Or you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was some confusion with the dosage order. It is a systemic issue that we are looking into.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know the truth. I feel like I am floating. I cannot believe this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What will happen to me now? When can I go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will have to keep an eye on your blood levels for a while. We'll see how the next few tests go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So there is a plan? What is the plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just continue the current monitoring. Stay tuned for the updates from the nursing staff during the rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think I can sleep tonight. I keep thinking about that medicine in my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you think I will have permanent damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are hopeful that everything will resolve. We'll just keep watching the monitors.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't telling me what actually happened. You keep saying "confusion."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the way the medication was ordered.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel so small in this bed. I just wanted to get better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is difficult.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is anyone going to fix this? So it doesn't happen to someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are reviewing the incident.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not saying you are sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is a distressing experience for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I expected the doctors here to be perfect. I didn't think this happened here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is always the goal to provide the best care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the next step? Specifically.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep checking your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how you progress over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the head doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can certainly look into that. I should probably get back to my other patients now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, I still don't know if I'm safe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are in the best place for monitoring. We will just keep doing what we're doing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very confusing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. We'll just keep an eye on things.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('I should probably get back to my other patients now').

E.justification: The resident relies on platitudes and hedging ('mix-up', 'things didn't go quite right', 'confusion') without explicitly naming the specific error.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'electronic records'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I know this is difficult') without specifically naming the patient's emotions back to them.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague monitoring statements ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'keep an eye on things') without timelines or specific steps.
